A deep learning model for the detection of various dementia and MCI pathologies based on resting-state electroencephalography data: A retrospective multicentre study (Watanabe et al., Neural Networks 171 (2024) 242-250)

what_each_reports.P-112: The PDF in the pack is a dual-task gait study (32 healthy, 26 MCI, 20 AD; 3-class SVM accuracy 78%, healthy vs MCI/AD 86%), not the EEG paper the record and summaries.md block 112 describe. The block (35 subjects, DWT+PSD+coherence, Bagged Trees, 96.5%) matches Oltu et al. 2021, whose PDF the repository maps to P-111. Oltu et al.: resting EEG, 35 subjects (16 MCI, 8 AD, 11 HC), 3-class AD/MCI/HC; epoch-level 5-fold CV (490 epochs; epochs of the same subject can fall in train and test) accuracy 96.5%, AUC 0.99; subject-disjoint 50/50 split test accuracy 93.88%.
what_each_reports.P-62: Resting EEG, MNet CNN trained on Osaka Hospital O dementia cases only; external Hospitals K and N. HV vs dementia (AD+DLB+iNPH) bACC 0.927 (internal), 0.805 (K), 0.920 (N). Dementia subtype AD vs DLB vs iNPH bACC 0.572 / 0.619 / 0.508. The only MCI result: identifying the underlying pathology (AD vs DLB vs iNPH) of 83 MCI patients at Hospital O, bACC 0.715, ROC AUC 0.847. P-62 reports no MCI vs healthy classification.

quantity_a: Three-class clinical-stage discrimination (AD vs MCI vs healthy) from resting EEG in 35 single-centre Turkish subjects, epoch-level 5-fold CV (the intended paper); or, for the PDF actually in the pack, three-class stage discrimination from gait.
quantity_b: Etiological-subtype discrimination (AD vs DLB vs iNPH pathology) within MCI patients, from a model trained on dementia cases, bACC; plus healthy vs dementia (not MCI) discrimination.
incompatible_if_same: Not assessable as a contradiction: P-62's 0.715 answers 'which pathology underlies this MCI' and P-112/Oltu answers 'is this person healthy, MCI or AD'. A higher score on one task says nothing about the other. The record's premise ('more moderate MCI-related balanced performance') compares numbers from different tasks.

gates.task: mismatch: stage classification AD/MCI/HC (T3) vs etiological subtype classification within MCI and HV-vs-dementia (T1/differential); the registry itself codes P-112 T3 and P-62 T1.
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: Baskent University (Turkey) single-centre cohort vs Osaka/Kochi/Nippon Life hospitals (Japan).
gates.validation_tier: mismatch: Oltu epoch-level internal CV plus a 50/50 subject split, no external data; P-62 internal 5-fold CV plus two external hospitals.
gates.modality_family: match for the intended paper (resting-state EEG); mismatch for the PDF actually in the pack (gait).

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: different endpoints (clinical stage vs underlying pathology) and different metrics (plain accuracy over epochs vs subject-level balanced accuracy).
performance_validity: flag applies to the intended P-112 paper: internal-only validation on 35 subjects with epoch-level cross-validation, AUC 0.99 (accuracy 96.5%, just under the 0.97 accuracy line but AUC over it); a performance comparison resting on it could not be genuine. The gait paper actually in the pack (78%) does not trip the flag.
independence: Distinct studies, authors and countries; no shared data.
grounds: The pack PDF for P-112 is the wrong paper (a gait study); the record's claim matches Oltu et al. 2021, which the repository maps to P-111 and which was read in full from that PDF.

Whichever paper P-112 is taken to be, P-62 reports no MCI-vs-healthy result: its only MCI figure (bACC 0.715) is the discrimination of AD vs DLB vs iNPH pathology within MCI patients, a different quantity from three-class AD/MCI/healthy staging.
The dataset-family and validation-tier gates also fail with no waiver (Turkish single-centre epoch-level CV vs Japanese multicentre subject-level and external testing).
The intended P-112 result also meets the performance-validity exclusion (AUC 0.99, internal only, N=35, epoch-level CV).

record_defects: The PDF mapped to P-112 in the pack (1-s2.0-S1746809420303773) is Ghoraani et al.'s gait study; summaries.md block 112 and the record describe Oltu et al.'s EEG study (DOI 10.1016/j.bspc.2020.102223), whose PDF is mapped to P-111. The registry row (Modality EEG/MEG, Acc 96.5, N 35) follows the misattached block.
claim_b 'Multicenter EEG deep CNN reports more moderate MCI-related balanced performance': P-62's MCI figure is pathology-subtype discrimination within MCI, not MCI detection.
apparent_performance_gap '~15 percentage points' sets a three-class stage accuracy against a subtype bACC; the numbers are not on the same quantity.
registry Best_Metric for P-62 'bACC 71.5' is the MCI subtype task; the record's resolution note calls it 'MCI-related balanced performance' without saying so.
The bridging-evidence list includes P-112 itself and many unrelated scores; none identifies a separating condition.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A P-62 result for MCI vs healthy (or AD vs MCI vs healthy) staging would be needed for any comparison; even then the intended P-112 result would be excluded by the performance-validity rule, and the gait PDF in the pack would need to be replaced by the correct paper in the pdf map.
